reviews.review: Picked this up during a sale and loved every minute of it, great for relaxing and carving through hordes of orks without having to worry about the complications of modern gaming. Its simple, but therein lies the beauty. It is a crime this game never recieved the sequel and kudos it deserved when it was first released.
Pretty damn good.  Graphics and storyline really put you in the game.  I would highly recommend to any Warhammer 40K fan out there.

This game is kinda short, but damn it was good !!!

If you like classic third person shooter with great story buy it , its worth it, I wish there was a sequel :(

Developers dont make them anymore how they used to :(

The sad fact is, this game places far, far too much focus on melee combat than is necessary, especially when your opposition is both stronger than you in melee combat, more numerous and features vastly superior ranged support than your ranged weapons can reliably dish out. The low-and-slow means of melee damage and inability to simply push through injuries results in every fight quickly turning into an uncomfortable meat grinder.

This is a significant flaw of the game; an inflexible concentration on melee weapons and combat, yet melee combat is punishing and tedious to engage in... and then, at the same time, it restricts your method of regaining health to melee executions! Executions themselves seem to have been advertised as magnificent and epic means of finishing off an enemy, yet it rapidly becomes a boring and even tiresome affair, especially since enemies can counteract your attempts to execute them. The function itself is largely unexplained, leading new and uncomfortable players ot blindly fumble at an "elite" melee opponent and receive a faceful of alien knuckle sandwich for their efforts.

Evidently, the designers wanted players to approach each level as though it were a river, constantly moving forward with little deviation from progress, yet the level design itself does not reflect this sentiment properly; the levels all have the one true path, obviously, but they go back and forth between being linear corridors and branching paths and sometimes arena zones and proper fortified staging areas, eliminating any concept of consistent level layout and causing no small amount of confusion and flow disruption.

The story, from what little of it I could grind my teeth through, came across as unimaginitive and stale, with very little genuine character from anybody and no clear long-term intent, seemingly just fabricating a big, empty pit to throw sword-swinging "Space Marines" into and then flood them with uninspired orkish clumps. The only Imperial Guard character who seemed to exist beyond the background was a woman, so I have an uncomfortable suspicion that the story would attempt to hamfist some kind of romantic subplot to thrust upon the player's mind, which on its own isn't typically an all too impressive move, but in the setting of the grim darkness of the 41st millenium just seems outright foolish, and all but flies directly in the face of the spirit of Warhammer 40,000. Make war, not love. (I would also like to make the "all's fair in love and war, and this ain't love" joke.)

For the designs of the marines themselves... maybe put some helmets on before you launch yourselves into an open aerial combat zone.

Speaking of which, the utterly flagrant disregard for the teachings of the Codex Astartes just to make your special helmet-less Space Marines seem like bad-*** mavericks and loose cannons who don't abide the rules because it gets in the way of how much booty they kick and how many names they take... is nothing short of shallow writing, and the kind of empty aggrandizement I would expect only from common fanfiction and Hollywood.

Which, in retrospect, is sort of how the game felt; like a bad Hollywood film. Flat characters, unclear goals, cookie cutter enemies and supporting cast, ferociously illogical tactics (you start out with a pistol and a large knife, for the record) and a great big bombastic 10,000ft high air battle with plenty of Michael Bay brand explosions and fast-moving objects.

As a final critique, I want to quickly address the orks themselves, as they're the ONLY enemies I wasted time fighting and never made it to the daemons I've been told are later on in the story. Their voices are painfully bad, and their lines repeat over and over and over again. It's not just pathetic; it's disgusting.

Which is sort of how I'd summarize the game. Less than pathetic. As someone who can enjoy getting their face kicked in as a Chaos Sorcerer in Eternal Crusade simply because of the setting logic (no matter who wins, I will be revived later by the dark gods and blood will have been spilled to please them, so I technically win), I feel confident in my judgement when I say that this game does NOT feel like a Warhammer 40,000 game. It feels like a really, really bad attempt to make a parody of Gears Of War... which, ironically enough, WAS a good franchise. Had their ups and downs, but each game had redeemable features.

This one does not.
